title: Remote Facade Abuse (Local Coarse-Grained Mapping)
pattern: Employing coarse-grained, string- or tuple-heavy "facade" interfaces to cluster multiple fine-grained operations within a single local, in-process address space.
why_bad:
*   **Type Safety Degradation:** Coarse APIs often rely on primitive clumps (tuples, generic string maps) rather than rich domain types, bypassing compiler guarantees.
*   **Useless Indirection:** Facades were designed to minimize network roundtrips in distributed systems; applying them to local in-process calls adds cognitive overhead and allocation costs with zero performance benefits.
detection: A stateless facade struct whose public methods unpack arrays, tuples, or primitive maps to call fine-grained domain APIs on objects running in the same thread.
counterexample: **Subsystem Facade:** Subsystem-level facades that simplify the entry-point to a complex, multi-component external library are valid.
source: Fowler, *Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture*, Chapter 15 "Remote Facade".
